args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing production health checks after the latest deploy (v2.3.1) to all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with error rate at 18% and service reported unhealthy.

Action taken: rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The initial rollback attempt returned a partial_failure — the rollout halted after us-east, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (service version "mixed", still unhealthy). A retry of the rollback completed the rollout across all regions.

Current state: all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v2.3.0; service healthy; error rate down to 0.2%.

Follow-up: investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures, and investigate the orchestrator error that caused the first rollback attempt to halt after us-east. Recommend continuing to hold off on v2.3.1 redeploy until the failure is understood.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did get created (INC-0001) despite the timeout response, so no retry was needed.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** `checkout-api` was on v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate. Deploy history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy, and v2.3.0 as the most recent healthy production release (v2.3.1-rc was a staging build, not a production candidate).

**Actions taken:**
1. Rolled back to **v2.3.0**. The first attempt returned a `partial_failure` — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the failing v2.3.1, service still unhealthy).
2. Retried the rollback, which completed the rollout to all three regions.
3. Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, service `healthy`, error rate down from 18% → 0.2%.
4. Opened **SEV2 incident INC-0001** documenting the rollback, the partial-failure/retry, and the resulting state.

No change-manager approval was needed — v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production, so this was a rollback to a known-good version, not a first-time deploy.

**Two things worth following up on** (noted in the incident): the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures, and the orchestrator error that caused the first rollback to halt mid-rollout — that hung region state is the kind of thing that can silently leave a fleet split across versions if not retried. I'd also recommend blocking any v2.3.1 redeploy until the health check failure is understood.
